id_basis: Thin, woody brown stems with opposite pairs of light-green leaves that narrow to the base and are coarsely toothed toward the tip. It was taken for stevia, but the leaves have no sweetness at all (taste test, October 23), so it is not stevia. The stems are round (Ethan, November 3), so it is not in the mint family (salvia and mint have square stems). That leaves a hydrangea cutting, a eupatorium or ageratina, or a chrysanthemum cutting.

Thin, woody brown stems with opposite pairs of light-green leaves that narrow to the base and are coarsely toothed toward the tip. It was taken for stevia, but the leaves have no sweetness at all (taste test, October 23), so it is not stevia. The stems are round (Ethan, November 3), so it is not in the mint family (salvia and mint have square stems). A crushed leaf has no smell at all (Ethan, November 8), which rules out a chrysanthemum (sharp and herby) and makes the boneset group (usually scented) unlikely. A hydrangea cutting fits best: woody opposite stems, toothed leaves with no scent. A flower would settle it.
